subject: sociology
source_note: Topic structure follows the Eduqas/WJEC GCSE Sociology specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships.

units.name: Understanding Social Processes
units.blurb: Culture, families, education and research methods

topics.name: Families
topics.blurb: Family diversity, change and sociological theories

topics.name: Education
topics.blurb: Theories, processes in schools and patterns of attainment

topics.name: Social Differentiation & Stratification
topics.blurb: Class, gender, ethnicity, power and inequality

topics.name: Crime & Deviance
topics.blurb: Social construction, control, patterns and theories

connections.why: The family is the primary agent of socialisation introduced in the key concepts
School is a secondary agent of socialisation transmitting culture
Family background strongly shapes patterns of educational attainment
Socialisation reproduces the class, gender and ethnic divisions of stratification
Inequality and life chances are central to explaining patterns of crime
The methods learned in Component 1 are applied to enquiry in Component 2
Studies of attainment rely on the research methods studied
Family structures both reflect and reproduce social inequality
Education is a key mechanism of social mobility and reproduction
Crime statistics are a worked example of interpreting sociological data
